verdict_line: Operating margin fell from 16.7% to 7.0% in the year it was spun out, and the CEO has publicly called untangling its parcel-centric technology "a massive effort." A transition services agreement expires around June 2028. The clearest carve-out mandate on the roster.

thesis.text: Margin collapsed through separation. FY2026 operating income fell 58.6% to $616 million on revenue of $8.8 billion (−1.1%) — an operating margin of 7.0% against 16.7% the prior year. Adjusted operating income $1.1 billion (−25.6%), adjusted margin 12.6%.

The technology separation is stated in the CEO's own words. John Smith has described how FedEx meshed back-office technology across units in 2009, that the majority of it was parcel-centric, and that unbundling it is, in his phrase, a massive effort.

The clock is contractual. A Transition Services Agreement with FedEx runs up to two years from the spin-off — to approximately June 2028 — covering order creation and network technology operations. Systems independence must be achieved before it lapses.

Pricing must now stand alone. Separation decouples parcel and LTL contracts, so LTL must be priced on its own merits without parcel volume subsidising the relationship — making yield management and customer profitability analytics first-order capabilities.

exhibits.title: The cost of independence
exhibits.headline: Operating margin fell from 16.7% to 7.0% and operating income dropped 58.6% in the separation year.
exhibits.body_html:
For FY2026 (year ended 31 May 2026): revenue $8.8 billion (−1.1%), operating income $616 million (−58.6%), adjusted operating income $1.1 billion (−25.6%). Q4 FY2026: revenue $2.4 billion (+4.8%), operating income $158 million (−66.9%), adjusted $363 million, average daily shipments 86,700 (−5.9%) with revenue per shipment $415.22 (+11.5%). Pre-spin the company took on $4.3 billion of debt ($3.7B senior notes plus a $0.6B term loan) with a $1.2 billion revolver. Shares outstanding 149,518,133 as at 3 August 2026.

Basis note: these are FedEx Freight segment results as reported within FedEx Corporation and are explicitly not presented on a carve-out basis, the 10-K's audited carve-out financials differ, and standalone full-year net income was not disclosed.
exhibits.sowhat: Revenue per shipment rose 11.5% while shipments fell 5.9% — they are already trading volume for yield. Doing that well without parcel cross-subsidy requires pricing science they have never had to own before.

exhibits.title: The separation clock
exhibits.headline: Independent since 1 June 2026, with a transition services agreement expiring around June 2028 and a seven-month transition period closing 31 December 2026.
exhibits.body_html: FedEx completed the spin-off on 1 June 2026, distributing 80.1% of FedEx Freight stock pro rata — one share for every two FedEx shares — and retaining 19.9%, which per the 10-K it must generally dispose of within 24 months. The company changed its fiscal year-end from 31 May to 31 December, so its first standalone reporting period is a seven-month transition period from 1 June to 31 December 2026. Guidance for that period: revenue growth of 4–6% against $5.1 billion, operating income $475–515 million, diluted EPS $1.75–1.95. President and CEO John A. Smith, CFO Marshall Witt, Chairman R. Brad Martin. Approximately 40,000 employees and 355+ terminals.
exhibits.sowhat: Three dated pressure points converge: first standalone results in early 2027, FedEx's 19.9% disposal within 24 months, and TSA expiry around June 2028. Everything about the technology estate has to be resolved inside that window.

sources.label: FedEx completes spin-off of FedEx Freight
